summary.text: 假 is conventionally analyzed as a phonosemantic compound: 亻 is assigned a person-related meaning and 叚 a sound role. A competing account proposes 人 was added to distinguish the graph from 叚. The character is attested with the meanings “false” and “borrow,” but their historical order is unresolved.

formation.text: The conventional analysis is phonosemantic: 亻 contributes a person-related meaning and 叚 supplies a sound cue. A competing proposal treats 人 as an addition distinguishing 假 from 叚 in Qin-period writing. The cited accounts do not resolve the difference.

components.text: 亻 is analyzed as the person-related element in the conventional account. Whether it is a side form of 人 or an addition distinguishing 假 from 叚 is not established by the cited graphic evidence.
叚 is conventionally analyzed as the phonetic component of 假. Accounts of 叚’s bronze forms and other uses concern that character and do not establish a graphic sequence for 假.

sound_limitation.text: The modern Mandarin reading match does not by itself establish the historical phonetic relationship or show that it applies to every reading of 假.

sound.text: In modern Mandarin metadata, 叚 is listed with readings xiá and jiǎ, while 假 is listed as jiǎ. This is a current reading comparison; the cited local data is not ancient phonological evidence.
In Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese notation, 叚 and 假 (the listed “borrow; false” reading) are both reconstructed *Cə.kˤraʔ. The same dataset gives a separate reconstruction for another reading of 假.

history.text: A scholarly account reports 叚 in excavated pre-Qin texts and 假 in Qin-period documents. It interprets a document dated to 221 BCE as distinguishing lending written with 叚 from borrowing written with 假, and proposes 人 as a differentiating addition. This remains a scholarly interpretation.
Later texts are reported to mix the spellings 叚 and 假. The cited material does not document a detailed sequence of dated graphic changes through later script styles.

Descriptions of 叚 analyze its bronze forms as 爪, 又, and 石, and record uses read as “blessing,” “fault,” interrogative words, and others. These accounts concern 叚; they do not establish an evolutionary path for 假.

uncertainties.text: The conventional analysis assigns 亻 a semantic role and 叚 a phonetic role; another proposal treats 人 as a differentiating addition. The cited evidence does not settle their relationship.
The evidence does not establish a dated development from “borrow” to “false.” A proposed path through “simulate” remains disputed.
A historical sound comparison is available for one reading in Baxter–Sagart’s reconstruction, but the cited evidence does not establish that it applies to every reading of 假.

senses.text: 假 is glossed as “not true,” and a cited classical example uses it to mean “false” or “not so.” The first occurrence is not securely dated in the cited material.

senses.period: classical text; composition and attestation dating unresolved
senses.text: A cited classical example uses 假 for borrowing a passage. The Qin-period distinction between lending written with 叚 and borrowing with 假 is a scholarly interpretation of a dated document.

senses.period: historical and current; first attestation unresolved
senses.text: Textual examples record temporary or acting uses, and modern definitions include “vacation.” The evidence does not establish when these uses arose or how they relate to “borrow” or “false.”

limitations.text: The cited senses establish neither their relative chronology nor a continuous semantic development. In particular, the proposed path from borrowing through simulation to falsehood remains disputed.

overview.text: 假 conventionally combines a person-related element with 叚 as a sound cue. It means “false” and is also used for “borrow,” but the order of these meanings is unresolved.

components.text: 亻 is assigned a person-related meaning in the conventional analysis; its graphic relation to 人 and proposed role as a differentiating addition remain uncertain.
叚 is conventionally treated as the sound component; the modern and reconstructed comparisons displayed here concern particular readings, not every use of 假.

relationships.text: In the conventional analysis of 假, 亻 contributes a person-related meaning; a competing account treats 人 as a differentiating addition.
The conventional analysis assigns 叚 the sound role. A Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction lists matching forms for 叚 and one reading of 假; this does not establish the role for every reading.
